home.tagline: I build and lead engineering teams shipping products used by millions, with deep React Native roots — at Sky, Shell, BP and Hargreaves Lansdown.
home.aboutText:
I'm Warren de Leon, a Software Engineering Manager. Most recently I led the Mobile Platform team at **Hargreaves Lansdown**, one of the UK's largest investment platforms.

Before HL, I spent over two years at **Sky** managing multiple engineering squads delivering mobile and web products used by millions of customers. I led teams within Sky's SAFe-based organisation, overseeing 10+ engineers across permanent, contract, and early-career roles.

My technical roots are in **React Native**. Since 2017, I've built and led teams delivering apps for **Sky, Shell, BP, and Chelsea FC**, among others. That hands-on experience with mobile architecture, CI/CD pipelines, and cross-platform delivery is what I bring to my leadership: I manage engineers with the context of someone who's been in the codebase.

Born and raised in **Barcelona** with Filipino heritage, I started my career there as a full stack developer and taught Android development across Europe as part of an international employability programme. Moving to the UK in 2016 added another perspective. That multicultural background, growing up between **Catalan**, **Spanish**, and **Filipino** cultures before building a career in **London**, shaped how I think about teams, communication, and inclusion.

My focus is on people: coaching, progression, honest feedback, and building squads where engineers do their best work. I've guided associate engineers from graduate programmes into confident, independent contributors, and I take that responsibility seriously.

When I'm not managing, I'm still building. This website is an **Astro** static site I built myself. My personal portfolio app is a React Native project with 75%+ test coverage, five-language internationalisation, and **Detox E2E testing**. I stay close to the craft because I believe the best engineering leaders never fully leave it.

about.heading: About Warren de Leon
about.intro:
I'm Warren de Leon, a Software Engineering Manager. I lead mobile teams and I still work in the codebase, mostly **React Native**.

Everything I write is below. It comes out of work I have actually done: React Native architecture, testing, mobile security, state management, Module Federation, and how to run a hiring process that doesn't waste everyone's time. Build-alongs and post-mortems, not think-pieces.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: This is the personal website of Warren de Leon. I keep what I collect to a minimum, never sell it, and never share it for advertising. This page explains what is gathered, why, and how to turn it off.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.body: I use two tools to see which posts land and how people find the site. Neither one is used to identify you.
records: The pages you visit and the link or search that brought you here
Your rough location (country), device type and browser
Actions such as switching theme or following a social link
analytics.tools: **Google Analytics**, run by Google, sets cookies and may process data outside the UK under Google's terms. **Umami** is privacy-friendly analytics I host myself: no cookies, no cross-site tracking, and the data never leaves my own server.
analytics.optout: Umami runs without cookies, but you can still switch it off in this browser.
analytics.statusOn: Umami is on in this browser.
analytics.statusOff: Umami is off in this browser.

newsletter.title: Newsletter
newsletter.body:
If you subscribe, I store your email address so I can send you new posts, and nothing else. I only email when there is something new.

The newsletter runs on Listmonk, software I host myself. Signing up uses double opt-in: you get one email to confirm, and you are only added once you click it.

Each email records whether it was opened and which links you clicked, so I can tell what is worth writing. Those links carry tags that show up in the analytics above.

Every email has an unsubscribe link. One click removes your address straight away.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.body: Your browser keeps a few small values: your theme and language choice, and — unless you have opted out — Google Analytics' cookies. Umami sets none.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask what data I hold about you, request a copy, or have it deleted. To leave the newsletter, the unsubscribe link in any email does it at once. For anything else, get in touch.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions about privacy, or a request about your data? Email me at privacy@warrendeleon.com.

scheduling.title: Booking a call
scheduling.body: The **Book a Call** page embeds a calendar from **Calendly**. If you book, Calendly collects the details you enter (name, email, and anything you add to the notes) under its own privacy policy, and it may set cookies inside the embed. I only receive the booking details, and I don't use them for anything except the call.

howTo.heading: How to work with me
helps: Say what you actually need up front. The blunt version saves us both a round trip.
Interrupt me even when I'm in headphones. They filter the office out, they're not a wall.
Book half an hour instead of writing the twelfth message in a thread.
Show me the half-formed version. It's easier to help with than a finished one that went the wrong way.
hurts: Jokes at the expense of my professionalism. If something has annoyed you, say the actual thing.
Assuming I'm fine because I've gone quiet.
Calling out of the blue for something that could have waited until tomorrow.
howTo.sub: Small things, mostly. They're what make a week easier.

feedback.heading: Feedback
paras: Write it down, so I can sit with it and answer properly rather than defensively. Be specific. And keep it about the work: disagree with me in the room, but anything about me, in private.
Under pressure I'll tell you when I've reached my limit rather than go quiet. If I have gone quiet near a deadline, ask me outright.
feedback.sub: In writing, please. I'm better on paper than on the spot.

personality.heading: My personality profile
personality.sub: A place to start a conversation, not a verdict.
personality.source: The figures in this section come from my own results on 16Personalities and the HEXACO-PI-R. Main 16Personalities test taken on 4 September 2026.
personality.traitsNote: The dotted line is the halfway mark. Four of the five sit within ten points of it, so none of this is a strong reading. The one that shows up most at work is the last: I stay fairly level when things go wrong, and I'd rather be told early than protected from it.
personality.agreeHeading: Patterns I recognise in both results
personality.agreeSource: I also took the [HEXACO-PI-R](https://hexaco.org/hexaco-online) on 5 September 2026. It uses a different model, but I recognise two patterns across the results and in how I work. HEXACO scores are set against a comparison-group average of 5.00, from a sample of Canadian university students.

agree.claim: I check things, and I keep going.
agree.means: I'll have checked the work before it reaches you. I also find it hard to call a thing finished, so tell me when it's good enough.

agree.claim: I'm direct, and I don't let things drop.
agree.means: Say it plainly and I'll take it well. If something has gone wrong between us, raise it rather than waiting for it to fade, because I won't have quietly moved on.

personality.locusHeading: Where I think work outcomes come from
personality.locusSource: These are the work results from 16Personalities' separate Locus of Control questionnaire. I've left out the personal and social results because their stated primary categories don't match their scores. The work report also mislabels the secondary category; the figures below follow the displayed scores. They're separate scores, not shares of a total, so they don't add up to 100%.
personality.locusNote: Mine points inward. I treat a result as mine to influence and I plan accordingly, which is useful when something needs owning and less useful when it's already owned by someone else. It shows up as being slow to hand things over. If I'm holding something that should be yours, say so and I'll let go of it.
personality.typeNote: In September 2024 the same questionnaire gave me Adventurer (ISFP-A), which tells you roughly how much weight the label deserves. The numbers underneath it are the part worth reading.
